actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry. (text: CR S1369-1370)

dimensions.assessment: Affects fertilizer manufacturers, wholesalers operating in the United States, and agricultural market participants who use reported data.
dimensions.evidence: each manufacturer or wholesaler of nitrogen, phosphorous, or potassium for use as fertilizer shall report to the Secretary at least weekly

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory weekly reporting burdens on manufacturers and wholesalers, while providing market transparency tools for farmers.
dimensions.evidence: provide timely, accurate, and reliable market information that can be readily understood by farmers and market participants

dimensions.assessment: Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to establish reporting and survey programs within Market News, but does not specify exact dollar figures for costs.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall establish a program within Market News of the Agricultural Marketing Service

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to add a new mandatory reporting section and regulatory oversight powers.
dimensions.evidence: amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to establish a mandatory price reporting program for fertilizer

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent weekly reporting requirements and mandatory biennial reviews by the Secretary.
dimensions.evidence: Not less frequently than once every 2 years, the Secretary shall review the information required to be reported

missing_information: Specific budget appropriations or financial costs for administering the new reporting program.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates a mandatory weekly price reporting program for fertilizer manufacturers and wholesalers, along with retail surveys, significantly increasing regulatory reporting requirements for parts of the agricultural supply chain while exempting cooperatives and non-manufacturer retailers.
